This sidesteps every escaping hazard (a label containing a 18 /// backtick, ${, or a quote cannot break the page), and a <script> element's 19 /// content is "raw text" so entities are not decoded — the source round-trips byte-for-byte. 20 /// This is safe because HTML-escapes every label (so < 21 /// becomes <), meaning the source can never contain </script>. 22 /// 23 /// 24 /// The source-sha256 provenance comment is emitted as the FIRST line (before 25 /// <!doctype html>) so the same \A-anchored reader that validates 26 /// diagram.md validates this file too (graph --check). A comment before the 27 /// doctype does not trigger quirks mode. 28 /// 29 /// 30 /// The renderer (Mermaid) and pan-zoom library load from a CDN, so the interactive view needs 31 /// internet the first time. GitHub will not execute the embedded script — this file is the 32 /// LOCAL artifact; diagram.md remains the portal artifact. Fully offline (inlined assets) 33 /// is a possible follow-up. 34 /// 35 /// 36 /// Legend overlay. A corner-anchored #legend <div> 37 /// (position: fixed), mirroring the existing #bar/#hint overlay divs, renders 38 /// 's content OUTSIDE the Mermaid SVG. A Mermaid-native 39 /// legend (a disconnected subgraph of colour-swatch nodes) was prototyped and rendered BROKEN — 40 /// dagre lays out a disconnected subgraph as a phantom extra "task" overlapping the real DAG — so 41 /// the overlay div is the only approach that renders correctly. Static HTML, not templated from 42 /// the Mermaid source, so it carries no bearing on source-sha256. 43 /// 44 /// 45 /// Task-container click target: a POST-RENDER SVG title-band overlay (issue #232/#233 46 /// superseded, issue #235). A Mermaid click directive never fires on a subgraph/cluster 47 /// element (upstream limitation; see remarks), and the first fix 48 /// attempt — an invisible anchor NODE inside the container — proved useless in practice: dagre 49 /// sizes and packs it into whatever gap its own layout leaves, which for a content-dense container 50 /// is a tiny, off-center sliver (measured: 0.44% of the container's area on a real 4-guardrail 51 /// task). The fix implemented here instead runs AFTER mermaid.render resolves: for every 52 /// g.cluster element whose id starts with task_, compute a full-width band from the 53 /// cluster's own bounding box down to just past its .cluster-label's bottom edge (Mermaid 54 /// always reserves this header strip above any leaf content, so it is empty BY CONSTRUCTION 55 /// regardless of how many guardrails/preflights the task has — unlike an interior anchor node) and 56 /// append a real <a href="..." target="_blank"><rect fill="transparent"></a> 57 /// spanning it. APPENDED, not inserted first: a cluster's only two original children are its 58 /// background <rect> then its .cluster-label group, so appending puts the 59 /// overlay last in paint order (on top, clickable) without moving in front of the label text 60 /// visually (the rect is transparent) and — because every leaf check node lives in an entirely 61 /// separate top-level SVG group from its own container's g.cluster — the overlay can never 62 /// occlude or be occluded by a leaf node's own click target either way. Mermaid always wraps a cluster's title 72 /// <div> to a hardcoded 200px width (the bundled mermaid@11.4.1's plain 73 /// flowchart cluster shape never overrides createText's width = 200 default, 74 /// regardless of the container's own — usually much wider — computed width), and dagre's layout 75 /// pass reserves the container's header-strip height BEFORE that wrapped height is known, so a 76 /// long kebab-case task name (hyphens are valid soft line-break points) that wraps to 2+ lines 77 /// prints past the reserved strip, overlapping the first leaf guardrail/preflight box positioned 78 /// directly below. No Mermaid config knob avoids this — flowchart.htmlLabels only toggles 79 /// the html-vs-svg-text label renderer, and 11.4.1 has no documented option for cluster-label 80 /// wrap width. The fix (the fixWrappedClusterLabels function, run AFTER 81 /// mermaid.render resolves and BEFORE the title-band overlay above, since the overlay's 82 /// band height depends on the label's — by then possibly shrunk — bounding box) re-wraps the 83 /// SAME text at up to the container's own width instead: since the container is normally already 84 /// wider than 200px, this almost always drops the label to one line, which needs LESS height than 85 /// the original wrap — never more — so no other node/edge/container ever needs to move. 5	namespace Guardrails.Integration.Tests;

7	/// <summary>
8	/// The composition-root wiring test for the live diagram (issue #120 doctrine). <c>OnTheFlyDiagramObserver</c>
9	/// (04-implement-diagram-observer) is implemented and independently unit-tested, but nothing in
10	/// <c>Guardrails.Cli.Commands.RunCommand</c> constructs or injects it yet — so a REAL <c>guardrails run</c>
11	/// never actually calls it, and a plan's <c>diagram.html</c> never reflects the run's progress or its settled
12	/// outcome. This drives the real CLI end-to-end (mirroring <c>PlanGuardrailPhaseTests</c>' <c>CommandFactory
13	/// .BuildRootCommand</c> + <see cref="StringConsoleIo"/> pattern) against a small script-only plan, then reads
14	/// the generated <c>diagram.html</c> off disk.
15	/// <para>
16	/// A real plan already carries <c>diagram.html</c> BEFORE it is ever run — <c>/plan-breakdown</c> writes it
17	/// once via <c>guardrails graph</c> (<c>Guardrails.Core.Breakdown.BreakdownManifest</c>). This fixture
18	/// reproduces exactly that starting state: an explicit <c>graph</c> invocation writes the plain static render
19	/// (no per-node status at all) BEFORE <c>run</c> ever executes.
20	/// </para>
21	/// <para>
22	/// RED on current code: <c>run</c> never touches <c>diagram.html</c>, so after a wholly-green run it is left
23	/// byte-for-byte the static render <c>graph</c> wrote above — no <c>#node-statuses</c> side-table at all, so
24	/// the settled-status assertion below fails. That failure is exactly the TDD red
25	/// <c>06-wire-diagramobserver-into-runcommand</c> turns green, by constructing <c>OnTheFlyDiagramObserver</c>
26	/// during the run AND adding a final, non-refreshing export at run end (mirroring <c>RunCommand</c>'s existing
27	/// <c>LogSiteRenderer.ExportSite</c> call for the analogous log site). This test deliberately does NOT
28	/// construct <c>OnTheFlyDiagramObserver</c> itself, and does NOT hand-wire the scheduler with it pre-injected
29	/// — either would make the test pass even though production code never wires it, which is exactly the
30	/// false-green issue #120 warns against.
31	/// </para>
32	/// </summary>
33	public sealed class DiagramLiveStatusWiringTests
34	{
35	    private static async Task<int> RunCliAsync(params string[] args)
36	    {
37	        var io = new StringConsoleIo();
38	        RootCommand root = CommandFactory.BuildRootCommand(io);
39	        return await root.Parse(args).InvokeAsync();
40	    }
